message.reasoning_content:
Now start the service in the background. Use setsid/nohup so it survives. Let me do it in one call: start, record PID, and check.

I'll use nohup with output to service.log, and echo PID. Then in a later call verify.
message.content: Now let me start the service in the background (detached, with PID recorded) and confirm it is listening.

function.name: shell
function.arguments:
{"command": "cd "$(pwd)"
rm -f service.log service.pid
nohup setsid python3 service.py >service.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
echo $! > service.pid
sleep 1
echo "launcher_pid=$(cat service.pid)"
ps -o pid,ppid,pgid,sess,cmd -p "$(cat service.pid)" || true
echo "--- service.log ---"
cat service.log
echo "--- listening sockets ---"
(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null || netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null) | grep -E '8765|Local' || true"}
